Lukanivka Manshurovo Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mykolaiv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Manshurovo was founded in 1848 as a Jewish farmers' colony, when 68 Jewish families settled there; the population grew to 873 by 1858, supported by a synagogue operating from 1863. Lacking agricultural expertise, colonists often rented their land to neighboring peasants in exchange for half the harvest; in 1870, a lustration commission stripped colonists of their arable land and hayfields, though home gardens and cattle pastures remained in their possession. During WWI and the Civil War, the community suffered pogroms, pillage, famine, and epidemics. A soap-making cooperative was established in 1921, and by 1929 Jewish residents worked in the 'Kotovsky' and 'Khleborob' kolkhozes; the community endured further famine in 1932–33 before being entirely destroyed during the Holocaust.
